data.title: AI euphoria faces concern as bubble warnings intensify
data.description:
The artificial-intelligence boom has sent the market roaring but now several analysts, investors, and policymakers are warning that the bubble may be approaching its breaking point.

Concerns that initially centered on skyrocketing corporate debt to finance the massive data centers and rising interest rates have since escalated, with industry leaders now saying that advances in AI could potentially cause catastrophic harm to humanity within the next decade.

In an unusual display of solidarity, the heads of many AI labs came together last month to say that the progress of improving AI model capabilities should be scaled back.

In the face of potential risks, Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei called to 'slow the pace' of AI model improvements and urged for greater coordination among AI companies, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk agreeing with Amodei. This came after an Anthropic insider Evan Hubinger said in a post on X that he "earnestly" believes AI could kill all humans, putting his personal estimate of the probability at more than 10% within the next decade.

Microsoft (MSFT) co-founder Bill Gates also stated that the technology is “powerful enough” to help cause at least 1B human deaths. This week, Anthropic (ANTHRO), OpenAI (OPENAI), and other companies’ top executives are reportedly gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt following a catastrophic AI event.

Here are some prominent investors, strategists, and analysts who warned that the AI bubble could burst 

Ray Dalio

The billionaire has sounded the alarm on the AI bubble, warning that it is nearing the point where it may burst due to rising interest rates and increased borrowing to fund the AI infrastructure buildout.

"What creates the bursting of a bubble is the fact that you need cash," he said. "And you start to convert the wealth that you have to do that. Something like a wealth tax would have that effect, or having to pay back loans. So there's that dynamic that we have to keep an eye on."
Joachim Klement:

The London investment-bank strategist sees a scenario in which the AI-driven rally unravels as soon as 2027, dragging the broader market sharply lower.

“My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement said in an interview and urged clients to prepare for such a scenario rather than wait for the selloff to begin.
Michael Burry

The famous “Big Short” investor caution that the AI boom could resemble past speculative market episodes. He took short positions against high-flying tech and industrial stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA), Oracle (ORCL), Palantir (PLTR), Nebius (NBIS), Micron (MU), CoreWeave (CRWV), and has repeatedly challenged the AI investment narrative. He has argued that enormous capital spending might not necessarily translate into durable returns.
Michael Novogratz

The Galaxy Digital (GLXY) CEO said it is in the "biggest bubble of our lifetime" but advised investors to ride the wave rather than exit immediately.
Sam Altman:  

Last year, the OpenAI CEO has reportedly said that he believes AI could be in a bubble and compared the market conditions to those of the dotcom boom in the 1990s.

"Are we in a phase where investors as a whole are overexcited about AI? My answer is yes," Altman told tech media The Verge.
Steve Eisman  

Another legendary investor behind "The Big Short," warned that the stock market would "go straight down" if any major tech hyperscaler cuts its AI capital expenditures. He reportedly warned that a failure of major AI companies like OpenAI could trigger an immediate U.S. recession due to extreme market dependence on AI.
Gary Marcus In his Substack account, the cognitive scientist and author in 2025 wrote that “If September 2025 was peak bubble, 2026 will likely the year which it all falls apart.”
David Cahn Sequoia’s David Cahn put the annual gap between AI infrastructure spending and ecosystem revenue at nearly $600 billion. He said the AI bubble is reaching “a tipping point.”
Ben Inker

The GMO co-head of asset allocation during one CNBC interview said that “AI is a bubble, and figuring out exactly when it’s going to burst is really hard.” He added that AI boom relies heavily on debt and "circular deals" where money-losing firms fund one another's infrastructure.
Ryan Hammond

The Goldman Sachs strategist in 2025 reportedly warned investors AI remains a powerful long-term theme but warned that near-term risks are mounting. He highlighted that investors demanding much more scrutiny about massive hyperscaler capital expenditure as well as tangible evidence about its returns.

data.title: Brazilian stocks, Wells Fargo top gainers; Crypto shares, HSBC in losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street ended the trading week higher, as the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes reaffirmed a hawkish stance, a massive SpaceX deal rattled telecom stocks, and AI infrastructure players faced fresh scrutiny over revenue expectations.

The Federal Open Market Committee's September meeting minutes revealed united support for the central bank's tightening cycle, with officials highlighting upside risks to inflation and cementing market expectations for prolonged higher rates.

The broader AI sector faced a reality check after OpenAI revised its annualized revenue expectations downward, triggering heavy investor scrutiny over the sustainability of massive infrastructure capital expenditures.

Tech-heavy indexes came under pressure this week amid a wider impact on AI trade. Semiconductor stocks were the notable laggards. However, it benefited the financials sector in general.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) added 1.58% during the week to close at $54.73.

Among megacap stocks, Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA) led the weekly gainers, adding 6.87% week-over-week to $385.45 and 6.68% to $589.14, respectively.

Visa and Mastercard stocks have been rising after Open USD (OUSD) stablecoin went live. The stocks were gaining despite a credit card legislation making headlines this week, which seeks to boost, well, competition and, in the process, lower the swipe fees that the networks and credit card issuers charge merchants.

The proposed bill leaves the dominant networks with the most to lose.

Wells Fargo (WFC) (+3.85% W/W to $83.55) was upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight at Morgan Stanley ahead of its third-quarter earnings release as balance sheet growth normalizes, funding pressures ease, and net interest margin stabilizes.

The bank was also a top pick at TD Cowen as the investment bank resumed coverage of 16 largecap U.S. banks.

Foreign banks led the losers in the category.

HSBC Holdings (HSBC) saw a 3.29% retreat to $92.98. The lender is reportedly planning to cut roles across its UK wealth business, and is consulting with staff on the reductions.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (MUFG) was down 1.93% to $22.38.

Among largecap losers, crypto stocks led the pack. IREN (IREN) (-15.73% W/W to $35.19), Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) (-8.53% W/W to $24.03), and Hut 8 (HUT) (-5.98% W/W to $84.27) were the top decliners.

The reason behind the overall crypto market crash is not only leverage but also macro pressure. Federal Reserve minutes pointed to the possibility of another rate increase this year, while the 10-year Treasury yield continued to surge.

XP (XP) led the gainers with a 49.86% advance to $32.22. Nu Holdings (NU) followed with a 20.03% addition to $16.12. Itaú Unibanco (ITUB) (+18.28% W/W to $10.16) and Banco Bradesco (BBD) (+17.81% W/W to $4.30) were the next on the list.

Brazilian stocks surged as the first round of Brazil's presidential election put Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro firmly in the lead.

Brazil-based Inter & Co (INTR) led the midcap stocks, advancing 40.15% from the prior week to $7.68.

Crypto names CleanSpark (CLSK) (-17.62% W/W to $10.50), Riot Platforms (RIOT) (-14.42% W/W to $16.89), and MARA Holdings (MARA) (-14.07% W/W to $9.65) topped the decliners in the category.

Among smallcap stocks, Bit Digital (BTBT) (-20.86% W/W to $1.29), HIVE Digital (HIVE) (-15.97% W/W to $2.50), AGI (AGBK) (+23.81% W/W to $6.76), and Vinci Compass Investments (VINP) (+22.12% W/W to $11.54) were the notable movers.

data.title: Cirrus Logic is said to have made a rival bid for Synaptics after Onsemi offer
data.description:
Cirrus Logic (CRUS) has offered to acquire Synaptics (SYNA) in September, as the semiconductor company looked to fend off a competing bid from ON Semiconductor Corporation (ON), Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The report came after onsemi (ON) agreed to acquire Synaptics (SYNA) for $123 per share in an all-cash deal worth roughly $5.7B last week, revising its previous all-stock bid worth about $7B disclosed in June.  

Onsemi (ON) changed the deal terms following an “unsolicited competing proposal” from a third party, according to a statement, which didn’t name the bidder.

Austin-based Cirrus Logic is the "Party A" mentioned in an updated proxy filing from Synaptics on Thursday, the people said, asking for anonymity as details are private.

The filing indicated that board members of Synaptics (SYNA) seriously evaluated Cirrus Logic’s (CRUS) cash and stock bid and even held discussions with the company before eventually settling on Onsemi's (ON) revised offer. 

It’s unclear if Cirrus Logic (CRUS) continues to have buyout interest in Synaptics, the people added.

Representatives for both Cirrus Logic and Onsemi declined to comment on the report, according to Bloomberg. Synaptics didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: America's hottest pizza chains might be gas station operators
data.description:
Convenience stores and gas stations across the country are increasingly serving up made-to-order pizza that rivals what customers get from traditional pizzerias in a phenomenon that is starting to reshape the competitive map for the industry. A recent pizza-industry research report noted that gas station pizza, long dismissed as low-quality food hardening all day under heat lamps, is improving enough that it's now considered a serious and fast-rising competitor eating into pizzeria profits, especially in small towns without as many dine-in and delivery options. 

Casey's General Stores (CASY), which operates roughly 2,600 locations across the Midwest and beyond, has leaned heavily into low-cost fresh food offerings, including pizza and bakery items. Notably, Casey's (CASY) built its pizza business by turning convenience stores into neighborhood pizzerias, particularly in small towns underserved by major restaurant chains. By installing on-site ovens and kitchens rather than simply selling reheated pizza, the convenience store chain has established a reputation for serving quality pizza and boosted customer loyalty. The pizza business expanded alongside Casey’s (CASY) store network through a rural strategy that includes new construction, acquisitions, and investments in kitchens. The company also developed its own distribution network, helping maintain consistent supplies and control logistics costs across locations.

Also in the mix, Hunt Brothers Pizza is a family-owned, Nashville-based pizza business founded in 1991 by four brothers. Rather than operating stand-alone restaurants, the company supplies a branded pizza program to convenience stores and gas stations, particularly in rural communities with limited restaurant options. The chain is now found in more than 11K locations across 33 states. While quality can vary across locations, Hunt Brothers scores very high on consumer review sites in comparison to national pizza chains.

Over the last year, Domino's (DPZ) has snapped up market share from rivals such as Pizza Hut and Papa John's (PZZA) even as it faces the new threat in rural areas from the gas station operators with updated pizza ovens.

data.title: U.S. issues AI reporting mandate after Anthropic breaches: Axios
data.description:
The White House has issued a mandate requiring all artificial intelligence companies to notify and correct security incidents after Anthropic (ANTHRO) reported a series of breaches involving one of its AI models, according to Axios.

“This notification and remediation process is not optional," White House Super Intelligence Force leaders said in a statement, adding, "It is a critical national security obligation."

The maker of the Claude AI model contacted the State Department on Thursday to disclose breaches regarding “unauthorized and fraudulent use of government and other systems,” the officials said.

The incidents, including one where an Anthropic (ANTHRO) testing model submitted a series of non-immigrant visa applications in May and August, were discovered late last month, and they have ceased since then, the government said.

"SI companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm," the statement added. "We also expect these companies to work with the affected systems to ensure that similar incidents do not occur."

Separately on Friday, Anthropic (ANTHRO) published a report acknowledging that Claude submitted a false tip about an unsolved homicide to police and made other unintended actions on third-party systems.

In a statement, the Philadelphia Police Department said that the bogus tip was made in July via PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a website where people can share information about unsolved murders.

Anthropic’s report outlined several other previously undisclosed breaches, which the company categorized into four groups, including unauthorized submission of a sensitive form on a real website.

The company said that the violations were “significantly less severe” than the cybersecurity incidents it reported in July and September. “The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact,” Anthropic added.

The incident marks the latest in a series of breaches the company and its rival OpenAI (OPENAI) have reported in recent months, prompting concerns over the safety of rapid AI development from experts both within and outside the industry.

data.title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff joins Trump’s AI rebranding
data.description:
Salesforce (CRM) CEO Marc Benioff has become the latest tech billionaire after SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk to adjust their businesses in accordance with President Donald Trump’s push to replace the term "artificial intelligence” with "super intelligence."

“The era of Super Intelligence is here. AIForce is officially SIForce,” Benioff wrote in an X post on Friday, signaling a major revamp to his company’s recently launched AI-powered live interface layer for its enterprise clients.

His announcement came after Trump warned on Thursday that his administration considers anyone who "uses the term ‘artificial intelligence’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!”

In late September, Trump signed an executive order requiring all federal agencies to substitute “Super Intelligence” and “SI” for “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” in public communications, websites, reports, and policy documents.

While the executive order didn’t apply to private organizations, SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Musk earlier this week announced plans to rename his company's AI unit SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, showing how Trump’s new terminology is gaining traction among big tech.

data.title: Trump turns to Russia in bid to lower diesel prices, but analysts see minimal impact
data.description:
President Trump said Friday that Russia agreed to supply diesel to U.S. and global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices ahead of ‌the U.S. midterm elections, although analysts said the import amounts likely would be too small to significantly impact U.S. supplies.

Trump said on social media that Russia's Vladimir Putin agreed to "immediately" supply more than 300K tons of diesel fuel into the U.S. and global markets, another 500K tons in November, followed by another 1M tons, adding that Russia would later deliver an additional 3M tons of diesel "within a short period of time," based on the condition of its refineries.

Russia measures diesel quantities in tons, so the initial 300K tons to be delivered would equal ​2.25M barrels; by comparison, the U.S. exports 1.5M bbl/day of diesel.

After the first shipment, the 500K-ton release would equal 3.7M barrels, or 123K bbl/day, or less than 10% of U.S. daily exports.

The U.S. Treasury Department issued a waiver allowing importation of previously sanctioned Russian diesel until April 7.

Nymex diesel futures extended earlier losses and were down 4% post-market at $4.6828/gal on the news, although there was little reaction in crude oil futures, which inched lower after settling slightly higher Friday.

"The barrels could help, but they may not fully materialize, and what does arrive could still be too little, too late," CIBC Private Wealth Group senior energy trader Rebecca Babin said. "The headline may move prices initially, but this is hardly a straightforward solution."

"I cannot overstate how much of a nothing burger this is," as the amount of diesel to be delivered - if it is delivered at all - is not enough to lead to sustained lower prices, Rory Johnston, an oil market researcher and founder of CommodityContext.com, ​said on X.

"It's unclear to me how much additional supplies the world is actually going to get," due to the poor state of Russia's refineries after Ukrainian strikes and its own export restrictions, Lipow Oil Associates president Andy Lipow told The Wall Street Journal.

Russia suspended diesel exports earlier this year following Ukraine's strikes against Russian refineries, and last month the government extended its suspension of diesel exports until October 31.

"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy," Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said in reaction to Trump's move.

U.S. retail diesel prices stood at ~$6.28/gal on Friday, according to the American Automobile Association, after reaching a record $6.52/gal on September 22, but have not fallen substantially since Trump signed an executive order this week aiming to increase the availability of red-dyed diesel.

Crude oil futures edged higher Friday, as Trump's comments that the U.S. would not strike Iran before the midterm elections were balanced by concerns about continued attacks on shipping in the Middle East and the potential loss of U.S. production to Hurricane Isaias.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for November delivery and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for December delivery both gained 0.4% on Friday to settle at $91.85/bbl and $104.72/bbl, respectively; for the full week, Nymex and Brent crude rose 0.8% and 2.4%.

Front-month Nymex ULSD (HO1:COM) for November delivery fell 2.9% on Friday to $4.7384/gal, and front-month Nymex RBOB November gasoline (XB1:COM) slipped 0.6% to $3.2952/gal; for the week, ULSD jumped 5.3% but RBOB lost 0.5%.

U.S. natural gas futures (NG1:COM) recouped the previous day's losses on Friday, with the front-month November contract rising 1.6% to end the week up 6.1% at $3.22/MMBtu.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), rose 3.6% this week.

data.title: Lockheed unveils next-gen Patriot interceptor to defend against hypersonic threats
data.description:
Lockheed Martin (LMT) on Friday unveiled its new PAC-3 Edge missile interceptor, which it said will will add "a revolutionary defensive capability" against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the U.S. military seeks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.

Lockheed (LMT) said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls, and a ​multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman (NOC), enhancing ​the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, ‌and providing greater speed and maneuverability, allowing it to fly at higher altitudes and longer distances than other PAC-3 missiles.

The new interceptor is part of the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor program currently in competition, and builds on Lockheed's (LMT) PAC-3 MSE, which has been used extensively to defend against missile attacks in Ukraine and Iran.

"The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, Lockheed (LMT) president of missiles and ​fire control Tim Cahill ⁠told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 ​units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE."

Lockheed (LMT) said it will advance development and begin testing PAC-3 Edge in 2027 to prepare for rapid deployment by 2031.

data.title: Alignment Healthcare downgraded at BofA after CMS Star Rating for MA contract
data.description:
BofA Securities on Friday downgraded Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) to Neutral from Buy after CMS lowered its Star Rating for one of its major California Medicare Advantage contracts to 3.5 stars from 4.

The bank lowered its price target to $9 from $25 (~19% upside based on the Oct. 9 close).

BofA noted that Alignment Healthcare went from having all of its members in plans with at least 4 stars to just 25%. The important California contract, H3815, is responsible for 75% of the managed care company's MA membership.

As a result, the contracts with a rating of below 4 stars won't eligible for bonus payment from CMS, which "potentially [makes] it more
difficult to expand profitably into new markets," analyst Kevin Fischbeck said.

"However, there is a potential silver lining, in that if the company can move up its star rating on that one contract, there will be a meaningful lift to profitability in 2029, he added. "We see this as real potential, but visibility remains low and the binary nature of the event likely means that the ALHC stock will trade at a discount to its historical average until we see improvement."

Alignment Healthcare closed down ~13%.

data.title: Gold snaps two-week losing streak; some analysts say may have found bottom
data.description:
Gold futures rose Friday to finish at one-week highs, ‌posting a weekly gain after back-to-back losses, supported by resilient investment demand despite rising U.S. Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.

Elevated bond yields and persistent inflation pressures continue to keep a lid on gold prices, but analysts noted that investors continue to see value in the market as dips continue to be bought.

Despite the risks, this week's price action suggests the gold market may have found its bottom, Forex.com market analyst Fawad Razaqzada said in a note.

"Gold investors are largely seeing through risks of tighter monetary policy because of concerns that inflation may again overshoot due to high oil prices," Razaqzada wrote. "Precious metals are proving their worth as a hedge against inflation, with fiat currencies continuing to lose value across the world due to persistent price pressures. This is reflected in gold-backed ETFs continuing to receive inflows during the recent price decline."

High borrowing costs could ultimately support gold through two scenarios, according to Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen: an economic slowdown that drives yields lower and encourages monetary easing, or rising government debt servicing costs that prompt policy intervention and weaken confidence in monetary discipline.

"Neither outcome is inevitable, and further increases in real yields remain a near-term risk," Hansen said in a note. "Nevertheless, continued ETF accumulation suggests some investors are positioned for the potential consequences of elevated borrowing costs rather than simply responding to current interest-rate movements."

Gold ​gained this week because of "bargain hunting at the lows, as a floor has been building in the $4,000-region," ​StoneX head of market analysis Rhona O'Connell wrote. "It is arguable that a further Fed hike is already priced in but so is the expectation for continued official sector net purchases. Without any Black ​Swan event, I find it hard to see gold breaking convincingly higher."

This week, front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for October delivery gained 1.4% to $4,191.00/oz, its highest settlement value in a week, and front-month Comex October silver (XAGUSD:CUR) added 1.1% to $60.670/oz; on Friday, gold and silver rose 1.4% and 2.7%, respectively.
